M1.name: Improper Credential Usage
M1.description: Hardcoded API tokens, keys, passwords, or credentials directly in binary or source code.

M2.name: Inadequate Supply Chain Security
M2.description: Vulnerable third-party libraries, compromised build pipelines, or untrusted dependencies.

M3.name: Insecure Authentication/Authorization
M3.description: Missing endpoint authorization, vulnerable exported components, or bypassable authentication schemes.

M4.name: Insufficient Input/Output Validation
M4.description: Unsanitized intent handling, SQL injection, path traversal, or command injection.

M5.name: Insecure Communication
M5.description: Cleartext HTTP traffic, lack of TLS verification, or missing network security configuration.

M6.name: Inadequate Privacy Controls
M6.description: Excessive or dangerous permissions, sensitive telemetry harvesting, or background surveillance.

M7.name: Insufficient Binary Protections
M7.description: Debuggable release builds, absence of code obfuscation, or tampering vulnerabilities.

M8.name: Security Misconfiguration
M8.description: Enabled backups (allowBackup=true), default credentials, or exported activities without permission controls.

M9.name: Insecure Data Storage
M9.description: Unencrypted local SQLite databases, world-readable shared preferences, or external storage exposure.

M10.name: Insufficient Cryptography
M10.description: Deprecated cryptographic algorithms, hardcoded IVs, or weak pseudorandom number generators.
